name: The Repair Compatibility Graph of a Cornerless Seed Is Complete Multipartite
statement: Let $S$ be a cornerless, irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor, and let $\mathcal R(S)=\{a\notin S:S\cup\{a\}\text{ is dismantlable ample}\}$. Label each repair by its unique acquired support $P(a)=\{f:a^{\{f\}}\in S\}$. For distinct $a,b\in\mathcal R(S)$, the opposite-layer lift $X_{a,b}=((S\cup\{b\})\times\{0\})\cup((S\cup\{a\})\times\{1\})$ is ample exactly when $P(a)\ne P(b)$. Whenever it is ample, it is a forbidden pc-minor with exactly the corners $(b,0)$ and $(a,1)$. Hence repair compatibility is the complete multipartite graph whose parts are the nonempty fibres of $P$, computable from Hamming neighbours without pc-minor tests.
proof: The two-repair ampleness criterion gives adjacency exactly when the support labels differ. If an old concept $z$ is a corner of $S\cup\{b\}$, its unique maximal cube must contain $b$: otherwise that cube lies in $S$ and contains every cube of $S$ through $z$, making $z$ a corner of the cornerless seed. Since $b\notin S\cup\{a\}$, this corner cube is not contained in the opposite section. The symmetric argument handles corners of $S\cup\{a\}$. Thus the no-reflected-corner conditions hold automatically, and the two-extension lift theorem gives forbiddenness and the exact corner set. Inequality of labels is precisely adjacency between different fibres, yielding the complete multipartite graph.
comments: Every edge of the compatibility graph certifies a forbidden pc-minor directly from the two local neighbour-direction signatures.
